## Block 41 — Event handlers, clones and weak handles, delivery modes, deadlock detection

**Goal:** an application written in the callback style of centrifuge-js, centrifuge-go or centrifuge-swift sets a handler per client or subscription instead of reading streams, with Block 15's guarantees kept in every delivery mode; it shares the client through clones and weak handles; and a handler that waits on its own client fails at once instead of hanging. Source: parity item 17, adopted by the owner (2026-11-06, late: "Each keeps Block 15's guarantees (delivered means taken, exactly once on recoverable channels); where a mode cannot keep one, its documentation states which one it gives up"), design A with C's trait ("Planned after Block 19", "Handlers (item 17)"; amended by D6).

**Dependencies:** Blocks 13 (calls), 15 (delivery, take-over), 28 (runtime handle), 30 (`ready()`), 33 (`close()`), 34 (codes), 37 (fake server double layout), 39 (take-over between stream kinds).

**Out of scope:**
- async handlers (centrifuge-rust `docs/spec.md` §9.5); handlers receiving the client or subscription handle (§4.4);
- `on_*` closures per kind; several handlers per object; removing a handler other than by taking a stream and dropping it;
- deadlock detection in the token, data and getState callbacks, and for stream consumers (§9.4: undetectable);
- strong and weak counts on `Client`; a `Subscription` keeping its client alive (Block 33);
- an `error` event for a panic; the browser adapter's modes (Block 44).

**Sub-increments** (one branch and PR each, in this order):

| Id | Value clause | Scenarios |
|---|---|---|
| 41a | As an app developer sharing a client across tasks and app state, I want clones and a weak handle, so that every part reaches the client without keeping it alive past its last owner | "Dropping one clone of a client leaves it running", "A weak handle upgrades only while a clone of the client is alive", "close on one clone closes every clone" |
| 41b | As an app developer porting callback code from centrifuge-js, I want a handler per client or subscription, so that events reach my code without a read loop while Block 15's guarantees hold | the untagged (Task) examples of the outlines; "A handler takes over the subscription's stream" |
| 41c | As an app developer running thousands of clients, I want handlers on the client's driver, so that no task or thread is added per client | the `@inline` examples |
| 41d | As an app developer whose handlers block, I want them on their own thread, and waits that would deadlock to fail at once, so that blocking neither stalls the runtime nor hangs | the `@thread` examples; the "Thread handler" scenarios |

**Decisions** (reviewer, 2026-11-08, delegated by the owner, after a three-amigos round table on the draft):
- **D1 API.** `pub trait ClientHandler: Send + 'static` and `pub trait SubscriptionHandler: Send + 'static`, each with `on_event(&mut self, event)`, whose default dispatches to one no-op method per variant taking its fields: `on_connecting(code, reason)`, `on_connected(client_id, transport, data)`, `on_disconnected`, `on_error`, `on_server_subscription(channel, event)`, `on_message`; `on_subscribing`, `on_subscribed`, `on_unsubscribed`, `on_publication`, `on_join`, `on_leave`. A blanket implementation for `FnMut(Event) + Send + 'static` closures overrides `on_event`. A field added later to the non-exhaustive `Connected` reaches `on_event` only; a new variant adds a defaulted method (minor, RFC 1105). Set with `ClientBuilder::handler`, `Client::set_handler`, `SubscriptionBuilder::handler` and `Subscription::set_handler`, each taking `impl …Handler`. Verified by the reviewer: an unannotated closure infers through the blanket implementation, and a struct of another crate implements the trait without a coherence error (serenity `EventHandler`, rdkafka `ClientContext`).
- **D2 Delivery modes.** `ClientBuilder::event_delivery(EventDelivery)`, a `#[non_exhaustive]` enum, `Default` = `Task`, per client. One consumer per client runs every handler of the client and of its subscriptions, one at a time, in `EventId` order. `Task`: a task spawned through the client's runtime handle (Block 28 D1). `Thread`: one thread named `ferrifuge-events`, inside the runtime context (`Handle::enter`), detached, ending after `close()` once its events are delivered; if it cannot start, the client fails as for a panic (D4). Both start at the first handler set. `Inline`: on the driver. Source: centrifuge-rust `docs/spec.md` §9.4. (On the browser target: amended by Block 44 D15.)
- **D3 Delivery rule.** An event counts as taken when its handler returns; a handler is one more consumer of the existing outbox (`StreamOpened`). An event handed to a handler and not yet returned is in flight: it is not withdrawn, and it still holds later messages (Block 15, in order); a connect or subscribe command sent meanwhile recovers from the position the event would move to; its return confirms that position, a panic voids it (a new `Input::EventHanded`). Take-over works both ways, as Block 15 and Block 39 D1: the in-flight event finishes with the old consumer, the untaken events move in order. No handler runs while a client lock is held. `Inline` gives up Block 15's "Timers keep running": while a handler runs, no timer fires, nothing is read and no ping is answered; its documentation says so. Under `Task` a handler that blocks holds a worker of the client's runtime: timers and pongs keep running on a multi-thread runtime, while on a current-thread runtime nothing else of the runtime runs until it returns; the documentation says so, and that handlers that block take `Thread` (Codex on #167).
- **D4 Panics.** `catch_unwind` around each call. A new `Input::HandlerPanicked { event, message }` withdraws the event and disconnects with code 2 (`BAD_PROTOCOL`), reason `exception in event handler: <message>`, without reconnecting (centrifuge-js 63ed73e README.md:1063-1072, `centrifuge.ts:1810-1813`). The handler is kept, so it still receives `disconnected` and `subscribing`; a panic while already disconnected changes nothing. Logged at WARN. The `Inline` driver survives (invariant I2). With `panic = abort` the process aborts, as documented. (On the browser target, where panics abort: amended by Block 44 D15.)
- **D5 Clones and weak handles.** `Client` holds an `Arc` of an owner whose `Drop` shuts the client down, so dropping the last clone closes it (Block 33 D4). `Client::downgrade()` gives a `WeakClient` (`Clone`, `Debug`) whose `upgrade()` gives a `Client` while a clone lives, `None` once every clone is dropped, and a closed client while clones live (tokio `WeakSender`, `bounded.rs:1576`, `:1665`). `close()` on one clone closes every clone. A `Subscription` still does not keep its client alive (Block 33 D3, D4). Handlers are dropped after close, once their events are delivered, which breaks reference cycles. The handler slot sits behind a `Mutex`, so `Client`'s auto traits are unchanged (cargo-semver-checks).
- **D6 Deadlock detection** (amends "Planned after Block 19", "Handlers (item 17)", for `Task` and `Thread`). A thread-local marker naming the client is set by a guard around each handler call, in every mode, and read at the first poll of every call future of `Client` and `Subscription` (Block 38's helpers included) and of `ready()`.
  - `Task` and `Inline`: a marked call fails at once. Measured by the reviewer on tokio 1.54.1 (multi-thread runtime, 2, 4 and 8 workers): a task that wakes another and then blocks its worker leaves the woken task in that worker's LIFO slot, which other workers do not steal, 10 stalls in 10 trials (0 with `block_in_place`); every call wakes the driver, so a `Task` handler blocking on a call would stall it. tokio's own `Handle::block_on` panics inside a task.
  - `Thread`: a marked wait fails when it can complete only through a message that an event of this client's handlers holds back: a sent call whose reply cannot be read because reading stopped on a full read-ahead, or a `ready()` or a call waiting for the connection or a subscription while such an event holds messages (centrifuge-rust §9.5). The recorded rule (a full read-ahead only) missed the second case.
  - Calls of another client never fail. A `close()` polled from a handler does not wait for its own handlers: under `Thread` it resolves once the driver stops, under `Task` and `Inline` once closing has started (centrifuge-rust §4.3).
  - A new `CallError` code 16, `codes::error::WOULD_DEADLOCK`, message "would deadlock: called from an event handler of this client" (14 is reserved and 15 is used, Block 34 D1). A failed call is abandoned as a dropped one is (Block 13).
- **D7 Version and docs.** No version bump: everything is additive (Block 27 D5, Block 35 D5). Changelog `Unreleased`: "Added": the traits, `EventDelivery`, the setters, `Client: Clone`, `downgrade`, `WeakClient`, error code 16, the new code-2 reason, `Input::EventHanded`, `Input::HandlerPanicked`; "Changed": dropping the last clone closes the client. The README gains a "Handlers" section after "States and events", and the codes rows. The rustdoc of `Client` ("Dropping the client disconnects it") and of `Client::ready` (code 3 for a closed client; Block 33 says 4) are corrected.
- **D8 Examples per sub-increment.** The outlines carry tagged `Examples` tables: 41b runs the untagged (`Task`) ones, 41c the `@inline` ones, 41d the `@thread` ones; the runner skips an example tag whose sub-increment is not implemented yet.

**Structural acceptance:** one thread named `ferrifuge-events` per `Thread` client, started at the first handler; the handlers dropped after close (a `Drop` flag); a handler calling every synchronous method under `Inline`; the marker restored after a panic; no `tokio::spawn` in the adapter (Block 28 D1 check); the Block 14 @P gates unchanged without handlers.

```gherkin
Feature: Event handlers

  @D
```

## Block 42 — TLA+ trace replay

**Goal:** the sans-IO core is replayed, step by step, against the traces centrifugal/centrifuge-rust generated from the Centrifugal SDK TLA+ model, so that a step where the core leaves the model's schedule fails CI naming the trace, the step and the value that differs (parity item 20, adopted by the owner, 2026-11-06, late; restores Block 16's "trace replay, optional, later").

**Dependencies:** Blocks 8 (emulated transports, a failed emulation request), 9–13 (subscriptions, tokens, recovery, server-side subscriptions, calls), 15 (delivery), 16 (harness layout, planted faults), 18 (frames of several commands), 19 (delta), 33 (`close()`), 36 (automatic batching, optimistic subscribes).

**Out of scope:**
- generating traces: they come from the model (`tla/sdk`, an internal Centrifugal Labs repository) through centrifuge-rust's `Replay.tla` and `cargo xtask tla-traces`, none of which is read;
- reading anything of centrifuge-rust but its `docs/spec.md`, `docs/api.md`, the trace data files and their README, and its `LICENSE` for the notice;
- replaying into the tokio adapter: the traces describe the core's steps;
- changing the client to fit the model: a divergence that is a defect is fixed in its own pull request (D10); one that follows a recorded Ferrifuge decision is recorded (D5) by a spec pull request;
- traces of a later centrifuge-rust commit: a new copy is a new decision, and re-derives D5 and D6.

**Decisions** (reviewer, 2026-11-08, delegated by the owner, after a three-amigos round table on the draft):
- **D1 Fixtures.** The 18 `traces/MC_*.jsonl`, `traces/README.md` and `bugs.jsonl` of `crates/centrifuge-client-core/tests/tla/` at centrifuge-rust 88d6edf178f6db370d8e6756d389c89bf100436b (model commit dd28e7f9, per their README) are copied byte for byte to `tests/fixtures/tla-traces/upstream/`, keeping their relative paths. In `tests/fixtures/tla-traces/` go centrifuge-rust's MIT text and copyright line (`LICENSE`) and a Ferrifuge README naming the source commit, the path, the model commit and each copied file's SHA-256, as the fossil vectors do. `LICENSE`'s "Exceptions" ("In the repository only") and `REUSE.toml` gain an entry; `.gitattributes` marks `upstream/**` binary. The crate's `include` already leaves `tests/` out of the package.
- **D2 Trace format, as read from the data.** One JSON object per line: `config`, `constants`, `states`, and `violated` in `bugs.jsonl`. Step n is `states[n]`. `states[0]` is `Init` with all 13 variables. Every later state holds its `act` and the variables it changed, each written whole. Steps carry no parameters. The replayer finds the channel from the callback that settles (`cbs`) for `Cb_*`, from the `sub` that changes for `App_*`, and from the head of `toC` for replies and pushes. A teardown may change several channels at once. The 663 traces have 4 to 40 states each, 8 151 in all.
- **D3 Replayer.** A test binary, `tests/tla_replay.rs`, builds one `Machine` per trace from `constants`. It uses JSON and default options, with one transport only: websocket when `Ordered` is true, http_stream when false, so no fallback occurs. Automatic batching is on, and `Input::Flush` is fed after each step's inputs, as the tokio driver does (Block 36 D2, D3).
  - `Chans` become client-side subscriptions, added at the start. `ServerChans` become server-side subscriptions granted at connect.
  - `Recoverable`, `Delta`, `GetState`, `SubToken` and `ConnToken` set the subscription options and the token, data and state sources.
  - The other constants bound the model's search; a trace whose `MapChans` or `SPChans` is not empty fails.

  The steps map as follows. An `act` with no mapping fails the trace.
  - `App_*` → `Connect`, `Disconnect`, `Close`, `Subscribe`, `Unsubscribe`, `RemoveSubscription` then `add_subscription` (`App_Replace`), `add_call` then `Call`.
  - `Env_Open` → `TransportOpened`.
  - `Env_Drop` → `TransportFailed` before the transport opened, `TransportClosed` after.
  - `Env_Timeout` → `TimerFired(ConnectTimeout)` or `SubscriptionTimerFired(SubscribeReply)`, according to the head of `pend`.
  - `Env_CallTimeout` → `CallTimerFired`.
  - `Env_WriteError` → `TransportClosed`, since a failed emulation request closes the transport (Block 8).
  - `Cb_*` → `TokenFetched`, `SubscriptionTokenFetched`, `SubscriptionStateFetched`.
  - `Sdk_ReconnectTimer` → `TimerFired(Reconnect)`; `Sdk_ResubscribeTimer` → `SubscriptionTimerFired(Resubscribe)`.
  - Reply and push steps → a `Frame` encoding the head of `toC`. Abstract codes map to: `temp` 100 with `temporary: true`, `perm` 403, `expired` 109, `already` 105, `unrec` 112. Unsubscribe codes: `terminal` 2000, `resub` 2500, `invalidate` 2502. Disconnect codes: `reconnect` 3001, `terminal` 3500, `invalidate` 3014.
  - `Srv_*` and `Env_TokenExpires` drive the replayer's simulated server and clock only.
  - `Sdk_SSDeliver` → `EventTaken` of the next recovered publication.
  - `Sdk_StartFlow` and `Sdk_SSSubscribed` → no input. Each run of them is checked together with the last step before it that has an input.

  Every other event is taken at once (`EventTaken`), as in the model's "queued deliveries first". A callback outcome or reply is inferred from the trace; if more than one outcome fits, the trace fails instead of the replayer choosing one.
- **D4 What is checked after each step or group of steps.** The model's state, built up from `Init`, is compared whole, not only the variables the step wrote:
  - the client's state;
  - each subscription's state, client-side and server-side;
  - the commands sent, field by field: kind, channel, token version, recover flag, epoch and offset, the reject-unrecovered flag, server-side positions in the connect. A connect command comes first. Within one group of steps, the commands of one channel keep their order; those of different channels may come in any order, since the order in which the model starts independent flows is a schedule choice (Ferrifuge's registry order is Block 36 D5's, checked by its tests). Each command of the model is matched to the core's command of the same channel and rank, and the replies use that match;
  - the callbacks started (token, data, getState);
  - the reconnect and resubscribe timers, armed or not (other timers are not compared);
  - the application's stream position (`app`: epoch, offset).

  An action of the core that the model lacks fails as a missing one does. Abstract values map one to one:
  - token version 0 is no token, and n is `t<n>`;
  - epoch -1 is none, 0 is the sentinel `_`, and n is `e<n>`.

  A mismatch fails with the configuration, the trace's line, the step's index and `act`, and the value with both sides.
- **D5 Recorded divergences.** Four schedules of the model differ from recorded Ferrifuge decisions. Each predicate is mechanical, on the trace. A trace that reaches one is checked up to that step, must differ there as recorded, and stops. If the core matches at that step, the trace fails.
  - **DV1** (Block 36 D5, item 31): at an `Env_Open` over websocket, a client-side subscription is `subscribing` with no resubscribe timer and no unsubscribe reply awaited for its channel, and needs no callback (no getState load without a position, no token fetch without a token). The core's frame carries those subscribes after the connect; the trace's carries the connect alone. 70 traces.
  - **DV2** (Block 9), over websocket:
    - `App_Unsubscribe` or `App_Replace` while a subscribe of the channel awaits its reply: the trace sends an unsubscribe at once, the core waits for the reply;
    - `Sdk_StartFlow` while an unsubscribe of the channel awaits its reply: the trace starts the flow, the core waits.

    3 traces.
  - **DV3** (Block 11): an `invalidate` (2502) unsubscribe push to a client-side subscription that holds a position. At that subscription's next subscribe command, the trace recovers from offset 0 and epoch `_`; the core sends no position. 16 traces.
  - **DV4** (Block 8): `Env_WriteError` of a subscribe over http_stream. The trace keeps the client connected and the subscription `subscribing` with a resubscribe timer; the core reconnects. 5 traces.

  The count of traces each predicate matches must equal the recorded one. 86 traces reach at least one (DV1 and DV2 both: 2, DV1 and DV3: 4, DV3 and DV4: 2); 577 reach none.
- **D6 Counterexamples.** Each of the 7 traces of `bugs.jsonl` must match up to its step and differ there as this table says, checked in the test. `VERIFY:` the table was derived from the data by the reviewer; 42b confirms each row against the trace before running the core, and stops and reports if a row is wrong.

  | Line | Config | Step | The trace, unlike the core | Shows |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | `bug_accept_stale_reply`, websocket | 7 `App_Unsubscribe` | sends an unsubscribe while the subscribe awaits its reply | DV2 |
  | 2 | `bug_invalidate_empty_epoch`, websocket | 4 `Env_Open` | sends the connect without the subscribe | DV1 |
  | 3 | `bug_no_unsub_defer`, http_stream | 7 `App_Unsubscribe` | sends an unsubscribe while the subscribe awaits its reply | the bug |
  | 4 | `bug_no_unsub_wait`, http_stream | 9 `Sdk_StartFlow`, checked with step 8 | sends a second subscribe while the first awaits its reply | the bug |
  | 5 | `bug_stale_flow_continuation`, http_stream | 9 `Cb_SubToken` | subscribes with the token fetched for the flow `unsubscribe()` ended | the bug |
  | 6 | `bug_stale_flow_continuation_ws`, websocket | 9 `Sdk_StartFlow`, checked with step 8 | starts a token fetch while step 7's unsubscribe awaits its reply | DV2 |
  | 7 | `bug_unsub_push_any_state`, websocket | 3 `Env_Open` | sends the connect without the subscribe | DV1 |

- **D7 Coverage.** What the replay checks, as read from the data:
  - no publication delivery. The one live publication (`MC_not_recoverable.jsonl` line 29, step 15) and the two recovered server-side ones (`MC_large.jsonl` line 37, steps 34 and 35) come after their trace's DV1 step (8 and 23), where the replay stops. None is a delta. `Sdk_Publication` and `Sdk_SSDeliver` are never replayed, and D8's zero-count rule leaves them out;
  - every websocket schedule where a client-side subscription that needs no callback is `subscribing` when the transport opens is DV1, and is checked only up to that open;
  - no refresh or sub_refresh is sent;
  - Block 9's deferral over emulation is reached only by counterexamples 3 and 4.

  The replay therefore checks the scheduling of connections, subscriptions, tokens, getState and server-side subscriptions, and the application's position only as connect and subscribe replies set it. Delivery, recovery and delta stay with Block 16's runners, and optimistic subscribes with Block 36's tests. The fixtures README says so.
- **D8 CI and layer.** The replay runs in the `test` job and the portability job of every pull request, with no time gate.
  - The test checks each copied file's SHA-256 against the README.
  - The run counts the steps replayed per `act` and the values compared per D4 kind; a count of 0 fails, except for `Sdk_Publication` and `Sdk_SSDeliver`, which D7 shows are never reached.
  - Layer `@P`, each scenario claimed with `// @P scenario:`, as Block 16's are. No new dependency.
- **D9 Public API.** None. A hook the replayer needs goes behind `__test-hooks`, `#[doc(hidden)]`, as in Block 16.
- **D10 Unsubscribing while a callback runs** (prerequisite pull request; amends Block 9). `unsubscribe()` or a removal while a subscription's flow waits for its data, token or getState callback sends an unsubscribe command. A later subscribe of the channel waits for its reply, as Block 9 says. Sources: centrifuge-js 63ed73e `subscription.ts` `_subscribe` sets `_inflight` before the callbacks, and `_setUnsubscribed` (:1067-1077) sends `_unsubscribe` then; the model and centrifuge-rust `docs/spec.md` §7.3 do the same. Without D10, `MC_get_state.jsonl` line 22, `MC_refresh.jsonl` line 13 and counterexamples 5 and 6 diverge at their unsubscribe.
- **D11 A subscribe flow's callback outlives a teardown** (prerequisite pull request; amends Blocks 9, 10 and 11). A lost transport, a server disconnect, a connect timeout or `disconnect()` no longer cancels the data, token or getState callback that a subscription's subscribe flow is waiting for. The flow stays in flight, so the next connection starts no second one, and the callback's answer is used:
  - a token is kept; getState's position is kept, with recovery on; the flow goes on to its next callback (the token after getState, data after the token) whatever the connection;
  - when the next step is the subscribe command and the client is not connected, the flow ends there. The next connection subscribes with the kept token and position, calling neither the token callback nor getState, and calls the data callback again, as before every subscribe (Block 9). An answer that arrives while connected sends the subscribe on that connection;
  - an empty token, or "unauthorized" from the token or data callback, unsubscribes with code 1 "unauthorized" and no retry, also while disconnected. D10's unsubscribe command goes only while connected;
  - any other failure emits its `error` event and arms the resubscribe backoff, which outlasts a reconnect (Block 10).

  Block 16's I5 allows these continuations after `disconnect()`, and the chaos runners (`tests/chaos.rs`, `tests/chaos_adapter.rs`) stop reporting them as I5 violations, in the same pull request. `unsubscribe()` and removal still make the answer stale (D10), and `close()` still acts on no answer (Block 33). Disconnect code 3014 still abandons the callback, so no token asked for before the invalidation is used (Block 11). A token refresh's fetch stays abandoned (Block 25 D3). Sources: centrifuge-js 63ed73e `subscription.ts` `_handleTokenResponse`, `_handleTokenError`, `_getDataAndSubscribe`, `_loadStreamState` and `_sendSubscribe` (854-910, 770-824), which check the flow and the state, not the connection; `centrifuge.ts` `_clearConnectedState` (952-967) and `_sendSubscribeCommands` (2290-2292); the model, with `infl` kept across the teardown. Without D11, `MC_tokens.jsonl` line 27, `MC_refresh.jsonl` lines 4 and 5, `MC_large.jsonl` lines 9 and 22 and `MC_large_emulation.jsonl` lines 10 and 11 diverge after their teardown.

**Sub-increments** (one branch and PR each, in this order; D10's and D11's pull requests, with core unit tests, come first, as Block 41d's prerequisite did):

| Id | Value clause | Scenarios |
|---|---|---|
| 42a | As a maintainer, I want the core replayed against the SDK model's traces, so that a step outside the model's schedule fails CI with the trace and step | "Every model trace replays into the core up to its recorded divergence", "The replayer reports a planted mismatch" |
| 42b | As a maintainer, I want each counterexample of a bug variant to diverge where recorded, so that the replay is shown to tell the model from its bugs where the schedule lets it | "Every counterexample of a bug variant diverges where recorded" |

