## Block 46 — Client publish debouncing

**Goal:** an application that publishes a fast-changing value (a cursor, a typing state, a slider) over a subscription on a namespace where Centrifugo PRO advises a debounce interval sends only the first value at once and the latest one per interval, per channel or per map key, so upstream traffic falls without code of its own, and every `publish().await` still reports what the server answered for the value that replaced it. Source: parity item 32, design A ("Planned after Block 19": "in the core, also for stream publishes (key ""); the first publish is sent at once; a superseded publish resolves with the result of the send that carried later data, never with a success before the server answers"; `ANALYSIS-PARITY.md`, branch `analysis/parity`, "32. Client publish debouncing"; reverses Block 0's exclusion, recorded in Block 0's "Reversed exclusions"); `client.proto:629-631`; centrifuge-js 63ed73e `src/subscription.ts:255-312`; Centrifugo's documentation, "Bandwidth optimizations" (`/docs/pro/bandwidth_optimizations#client-publish-debouncing`).

**Dependencies:** Blocks 0 (references, precedence, test layers), 7 (Protobuf), 9 (subscription lifecycle), 13 (calls, phases, write queue, `CallError`), 14 (footprint gates), 15 (a reply settles its call when read), 16 (validation harness, I6), 18 (explicit batches), 20 (semver check, changelog), 21 (logging), 31 (statistics), 33 (`close()`), 34 (table of codes), 36 (automatic batching, its opt-in on the core), 38 (JSON helpers), 41 (deadlock detection), 44 (browser target, its timers and clocks), 45 (`map_publish`, `map_remove`, map subscribe replies).

**Out of scope:**
- a debounce on `Client::publish`, `Client::map_publish`, `Client::map_remove`, `rpc` and `send` (D1);
- server-side subscriptions: they have no publish method (Block 12), so a `publish_debounce` in `ConnectResult.subs` is not read;
- an application-chosen interval or a client-side debounce on a namespace that advises none (D1);
- a debounce on a map subscription's load: only its publishes and removes;
- merging a value into a send already handed to the write queue, a batch or the output buffer (D7);
- counter-measures to timer throttling in hidden tabs (D14; Block 44 D16);
- the in-memory server double (Block 37) and the TLA+ trace replay (Block 42), neither of which models this; the chaos runners cover stream subscriptions only, as Block 45 keeps map subscriptions out of them.

This block reverses Block 0's exclusion of client publish debouncing (owner decision, 2026-11-06, late, item 32); Block 0's "Reversed exclusions" gains its row, and the Block 0, Block 13 and Block 18 out-of-scope lines point here (Block 45's, "a map subscription ignores `publish_debounce` until Block 46", already does). It amends Block 16's I6 (D6) and Block 34 D1 and its `error` table (D10), as listed after this block.

**Sub-increments** (one branch and PR each, in this order):

| Id | Value clause | Scenarios |
|---|---|---|
| 46a | As an app developer publishing a fast-changing value on a Centrifugo PRO namespace that advises a debounce interval, I want my subscription's publishes merged to the first value at once and the latest per interval, with each publish reporting the server's answer for the value that replaced it, so that upstream traffic falls with no code of mine and no publish claims a success the server has not given | "Publishes within the interval are merged and the latest is sent when it ends", "A window with nothing to send closes", "A window stays open while it keeps sending", "A stale debounce timer is ignored", "An interval longer than the call timeout is clamped", "A publish made while subscribing is debounced once subscribed", "Without an interval every publish is sent", "A later subscribe reply without an interval turns debouncing off", "A superseded publish waits for the send that replaced it", "A superseded publish fails with the error of the send that replaced it", "A publish the server refuses at once keeps its own result", "Client-level publishes are not debounced", "Leaving subscribed drops what a window holds", "A window dropped by a reconnect is not resent", "A trailing send lost with its transport fails the publishes that followed it", "A trailing send waits for room in the write queue", "A trailing send is held by an open batch", "Trailing sends of a burst share a frame with automatic batching", "Dropping a publish withdraws its data only when no other publish waits for it", "A Thread handler's publish waiting in a window is not a would-be deadlock", "Publishing without Centrifugo PRO sends every publish", "A closed window frees its memory", "Waking with many open windows is reported" |
| 46b | As an app developer writing keys of a map channel, I want each key debounced on its own, and a remove to cancel the key's pending publish, so that a chatty key never starves a quiet one and a remove is never undone by a trailing publish | "Each map key has its own window", "A remove cancels the key's pending publish and settles the publishes it replaced", "Client-level map writes are not debounced", "A map subscribe reply's interval is honoured" |
| 46c | As a maintainer, I want debounced subscriptions in both validation runners, so that the interleavings of windows with reconnects and batches are checked as the rest of the client is | "Seeded chaos with debounced publishes on the core keeps every invariant", "The core runner reports a planted debounce fault", "Seeded chaos with debounced publishes on the tokio client keeps the invariants" |

**Decisions** (reviewer, 2026-11-09, delegated by the owner, after a three-amigos round table on the draft):

- **D1 API: server-driven and transparent, no new public method or option.** The interval is the server's, and `Subscription::publish`, `publish_json`, `MapSubscription::publish`, `publish_json` and `remove` apply it. No `SubscriptionBuilder::publish_debounce`, no `publish_debounced`. Reasons: `client.proto:629-630` tells the SDK to debounce; Centrifugo's documentation describes it as the SDK's behaviour; centrifuge-js has no knob; a server-provided parameter applied inside the client, with no per-call opt-in, is the common form of server-advised behaviour (gRPC service config, Kafka's `throttle_time_ms` in librdkafka). Only the subscription-level calls are debounced, as `client.proto` says "client publications" while the documentation says "when publishing via the subscription object" and centrifuge-js documents the client methods as undebounced. No opt-out in v1: centrifuge-js has none, `client.proto` says "should", and an application that must not have a value merged has `Client::publish` and `Client::map_publish`, which the README says; an option can be added later without a break.
- **D2 Interval.** `SubscribeResult.publish_debounce` (field 19), JSON key `publish_debounce`, is decoded in both codecs; `wire::SubscribeResult` gains the field, zero and absent both meaning "none". It is read from every reply that takes the subscription to `subscribed` (the stream subscribe reply, `subscribe_succeeded`; the map flow's two live-phase replies, `map_flow.rs`, centrifuge `client_map.go:1062-1063`), before the calls waiting for `subscribed` start (`subscription_calls_subscribed`), and replaces the previous value, 0 included: Block 0 precedence, `client.proto` ("When > 0") over centrifuge-js's "keep the old one" (`subscription.ts:573`, `:2626`), reported here as a divergence. The effective interval is `min(publish_debounce, Config::timeout)`: a wrong or hostile interval (`uint32` milliseconds, up to 49 days) cannot leave a call waiting longer than a phase of Block 13 may (D6); the proto's "should" allows the bound, and at the documented scale (`"50ms"`) it never bites. An effective interval of 0 means no debounce and costs nothing.
- **D3 Window, per subscription and key.** The key is the map key, or `""` on a stream subscription. With an interval, a debounced publish that passes the gate (below):
  - with no open window for the key: continues on Block 13's path as now, and a window of the interval opens for the key;
  - with an open window: the call moves to the new `Phase::Debounced`, its data becomes the window's latest, replacing the earlier latest, which is freed at once, and its caller waits (D4). The timer is not reset.

  When the window's timer fires: with a latest value, the latest is handed to Block 13's path, past the gate, as a new internal call of the subscription (D4), and a new window opens; with none, the window closes and no timer remains. So: one send at the leading edge, then at most one per interval while values keep coming, the last value always sent, as centrifuge-js's two timers do (`:265-291`; its second-firing branch is equivalent to a new window). The window opens at the hand-off, not when the frame is written, as centrifuge-js's timer starts at `_debouncedPublish`.

  **The gate** is at the top of `start_call`, for a call with a subscription whose request is `Publish` or (`unstable`) `MapPublish`: so a publish made while `subscribing` waits as Block 13 says and meets the gate when subscribed, in call order, the first one leading (centrifuge-js checks `_debounceMs` after `await this._methodCall()`, `:2879-2883`). `MapRemove` meets it too, for D12. Publishes through `Client` have no subscription and never meet it. A call released by a new connection or by room goes through `send_call` and `calls_connected`, not `start_call`, so a leading publish that waited is not debounced twice.
- **D4 Results (binding, "Planned after Block 19").** A publish that goes at the leading edge settles with its own reply, as any call. A publish that goes into a window settles with the result of the send that carried later data:
  - a publish replaced in the window, and the last one in it, follow the same trailing send: on its result, each `Action::CallSettled` is emitted for them, in the order they were made; a window's success is never reported before the server answered that send;
  - the trailing send's error reaches each of them with its code, message and `temporary`, as any reply (Block 13);
  - the trailing send is an internal `Call` no owner awaits, with the subscription of its waiters; `settle_call` emits `CallSettled` for its waiters and none for itself, so `CallSettled` only ever names `CallId`s the owner added. Its `SetCallTimer` and `CancelCallTimer` carry its own id, which the owner feeds back as for any call. The future each caller awaits is unchanged.

  Diverges from centrifuge-js (`:261`, `{}` at once; errors swallowed, `:278`, `:289`) and from the documentation's "every `publish()` call resolves immediately" by the owner's decision: Block 0 puts neither above it (the spec and `client.proto` say nothing about what a merged publish returns), and a future that resolves `Ok` has been answered by the server, as every other call's does (Block 13).
- **D5 Timers on the sans-IO core.** The core has no clock (`Machine` reads none), so one per-subscription timer with a deadline per key is not possible: there is one timer per open window, the design "a debounce timer per subscription and key" of `ANALYSIS-PARITY.md`. New in the public `machine` API, additive (`Input` and `Action` are `#[non_exhaustive]`, Blocks 17 and 45):
  - `pub struct DebounceTimer(u64)`: opaque, `Copy`, `Eq`, `Hash`, `Debug`, a number never reused by a machine;
  - `Action::SetDebounceTimer(DebounceTimer, Duration)`, `Action::CancelDebounceTimer(DebounceTimer)`;
  - `Input::DebounceTimerFired(DebounceTimer)`: a timer whose window is gone is ignored, as a stale call timer is (`call_timer_fired`), since the number is not reused;
  - `Machine::with_publish_debounce(self) -> Self`, `#[must_use]`, as `with_automatic_batching` (Block 36 D2): without it the core ignores `publish_debounce` and sends every publish. An owner written before this block ignores `Action::SetDebounceTimer` (`Action` is `#[non_exhaustive]` since Block 45, so it still compiles), its windows would never end and a parked publish, which has no timer (D6), would hang: the same silent failure Block 36 D2 avoids. Both adapters turn it on (`adapter/client.rs`, beside `with_automatic_batching`); the core runner and the @E scenarios use it.

  The driver keeps them in a `KeyedTimers<DebounceTimer>` on both targets. No `TimerKey` variant for Block 25's setting bookkeeping: a number is never set twice, and the machine ignores a number it no longer knows. No `ShortenTimer` counterpart: a window is at most `Config::timeout`. An idle client holds no timer (the Block 14 scenario "An idle client wakes only for pings and refreshes" is unchanged): timers exist only while a window is open. A new `KeyedTimers::fired_all` resolves with every timer ready at that poll, and the driver feeds them all before its next flush: windows that end together cost one iteration and one flush, not one each (a burst of N keys would otherwise be O(N²) `Sleep` polls, `fired` restarting its scan per timer), and D9's shared frame holds on the driver. Cost: a wakeup polls every open timer, as `fired` does for call timers; a client with thousands of open key windows pays it, reported by "Waking with many open windows is reported". A timing wheel (`tokio_util::time::DelayQueue`) or a cap on windows are ways out without an API change, should that report ask for one.
- **D6 Deadlines.** A window is a wait of a call, and Block 13 says each wait is bounded by `Config::timeout`. The clamp of D2 is the bound: a parked publish waits for at most `Config::timeout`, so it has no timer of its own and `Phase::Debounced` has none. After the window, its result is the trailing send's, itself bounded by Block 13's phases (connection, room, held, reply), so a debounced publish settles within 1 × `Config::timeout` more than Block 16 I6's bound, 5 × at most. I6 gains a debounce window among its waits (a chain of windows cannot arise: a publish follows only the trailing send of the window it waited in). Block 13's "subscription-level call waits for `subscribed`" is unchanged, as the window only starts after it.
- **D7 Write queue (Block 13).** A trailing send takes Block 13's path like any call: sent at once when connected and it fits, otherwise waiting for room (in line, its deadline running, `Config::write_queue_bytes` counting its frame once framed), for the connection when the transport is closing. The window keeps its own timing meanwhile. A trailing send is not merged again once handed over: a call waiting for room is already "sent" as far as the debounce is concerned, as with centrifuge-js, which hands it to `_centrifuge.publish` directly (`:275-278`); a window that ends while the previous trailing send still waits for room makes one more, in FIFO order, bounded by its callers' deadlines. Data held in a window is one value per key, the latest, and is not counted against `Config::write_queue_bytes`, like a queued call's data; it never exceeds what the application's own unsettled futures hold, and is freed when a window ends or the subscription leaves `subscribed`.
- **D8 Explicit batches (Block 18).** A leading or trailing send meets `start_call`'s Block 18 check as any call: while a batch is open it is `Held`, with Block 18's deadline. The window's timer runs regardless: a batch does not hold back the interval. A `Batch` with several publishes of a key: the first is held, the rest are merged in the window, and the trailing send is held in turn if the batch is still open when the window ends (else sent then). Block 18 D2 is unchanged.
- **D9 Automatic batching (Block 36).** A trailing send goes into the output buffer as any call and is flushed at the next `Input::Flush`: the driver feeds it at the top of its next iteration (Block 36 D3), so a window ending alone costs no extra wait, and windows ending together (`fired_all`, D5) share a frame, within `Config::batch_frame_bytes`. A sans-IO owner feeds `Flush` itself (Block 36 D2).
- **D10 Leaving `subscribed`** (centrifuge-js `:476`, `:1097`; documentation: "the SDK drops all pending publishes"). Every transition out of `subscribed` drops every window of the subscription and cancels their timers: entering `unsubscribed` (`set_unsubscribed`), entering `subscribing` on a lost transport (`subscriptions_disconnected`), on a server unsubscribe from code 2500 (`server_unsubscribe`) and on a delta failure (`delta_failed`). Map subscriptions leave `subscribed` through the same functions. Data waiting in a window is never sent: a resubscribe does not send stale data. The publishes waiting in a window fail:

  | Cause | Code | Message | Block |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | the subscription enters `unsubscribed` | 7 `SUBSCRIPTION_UNSUBSCRIBED` | "subscription unsubscribed" | 13 |
  | the client enters `disconnected` (`fail_calls_disconnected` already runs before `subscriptions_disconnected`) | 3 `DISCONNECTED` | "disconnected" | 13 |
  | `close()` | 4 `CLIENT_CLOSED` | "client closed" | 33 |
  | the subscription enters `subscribing` (transport lost, server resubscribe, delta failure) while the client stays up | **17 `PUBLISH_DROPPED`, new** | "publish dropped" | here |

  Code 17 is new because the case is new: under Block 13 a call waiting for `subscribed` survives a move to `subscribing`, so no existing wait ends this way, and 11 "connection closed" means "the reply cannot arrive", possibly applied. Code 17 means "never sent; safe to publish again after `subscribed`". 11 would be wrong on a live connection and says the reply cannot arrive, 7 says the subscription is gone. `codes::error::PUBLISH_DROPPED: u32 = 17` (14 reserved, 15 and 16 used, Block 34 D1; centrifuge-js `codes.ts` stops at 14), `temporary` false. Block 34's `error` table gains its row (README and `codes` documentation, the D3 test), with "the call fails; publish again when subscribed".

  A trailing send already handed over stays a Block 13 call, and its waiting callers follow it: lost as Block 13 says if it was sent (code 11), kept if it was waiting for the connection or room, across a reconnect, until `Config::timeout` of that phase, and failing with code 7 if its subscription becomes `unsubscribed` first (`subscription_calls_unsubscribed`). A publish at the leading edge is unaffected: it is an ordinary call in flight.
- **D11 A dropped publish future** (Block 13: "abandoned … never sent if it was queued"). `Input::CallAbandoned` of a publish in a window removes the caller; if no caller remains, the latest is dropped and the window goes on with nothing to send. If callers remain, the latest is still sent for them, the dropped caller's value included if it was last: an earlier caller's publish was replaced by that value, and it waits for that value's result (D4). For a publish that follows a trailing send: if none remains and the send has not been handed to the transport, the send is abandoned as Block 13's rule says (never sent); if the send is out, its reply is ignored. A remove that closed a window (D12) is the send its followers wait for: `Input::CallAbandoned` of that remove while any publish follows it removes only its owner, so it still goes out, or stays out, under its own call timers, and its result settles the followers alone, with no `CallSettled` for the remove. When its last follower is then abandoned, the follower clause above applies. With no follower at the abandon, it is an ordinary abandoned call (Block 13).
- **D12 Block 45: map subscriptions.** `MapSubscription::publish(key, data)` is debounced per key, each key with its own window, so a chatty key cannot delay a quiet one (`:2900-2902`). `MapSubscription::remove(key)`, at the gate after `subscribed`: if the key has an open window, the window closes, its timer is cancelled, its latest data is dropped; the publishes that waited in it follow the remove's result (the remove is the later operation on the key: D4's "send that carried later data", the data being "none"). On its result the followers settle first, in the order they were made, and the remove last, as it was made after them. The remove itself is sent at once, undebounced, and opens no window; a following publish of the key therefore finds no window and is sent at once (`:2908-2910`). A publish already in flight keeps its reply: on the wire it is before the remove. `Client::map_publish` and `Client::map_remove` are not debounced (`centrifuge.ts:566-567`, `:579-580`). The key `""` means the stream key only on a stream subscription; on a map subscription it is a key, refused by the server as ever (Block 45: 107). `#[cfg(feature = "unstable")]` covers only `MapPublish` and `MapRemove` handling; the window table and timers are unconditional.
- **D13 Block 41: deadlock detection.** `call_wait(id)` reports a publish in a window as `Other` (Block 41 D6: only a timer completes it), and a follower as the phase of its trailing send (`Queued`: `Message`; `Sent`: `Reply`; otherwise `Other`). Under `Inline` and `Task` a call from a handler fails at its first poll whatever it is (Block 41 D6), so debouncing changes nothing there; under `Thread` a publish in a window is not held back by the handler's event and completes.
- **D14 Browser target (Block 44).** Nothing in the core or the `Action`s differs by target. The driver arms a debounce timer with `platform::sleep` (gloo-timers, Block 44 D4; the `i32::MAX` cap never bites thanks to D2). In a hidden tab, browsers throttle `setTimeout` (about once a second, or once a minute when intensively throttled, Block 44 D16): trailing sends and windows lag by that much, and fewer values go out, the latest still kept. A frozen page holds its windows and timers until it resumes. Documented, no counter-measure (Block 44 D16). No `MaybeSend` changes: the public futures are the same.
- **D15 Observability and memory.** No new `Statistics` field: `messages_out` and `bytes_out` count what is written (Block 31), so a merged publish costs nothing. No log record carries the data (Block 21); no new record. One value per key stays in `Debounced` until a window ends: `Machine` adds a `HashMap` per subscription only when an interval is on, `Option<Box<_>>` otherwise, so the Block 14 subscription footprint gates are unchanged.
- **D16 Harness (46c, Block 16).** Both runners feed a `publish_debounce` of 1 to 3 × a tick (50 ms, so 50 to 150 ms) on some subscribes, a publish burst operation on those, and the core runner feeds `DebounceTimerFired` from the simulated clock. The runners use stream subscriptions only (Block 45). New invariant **I12**, core, after every step, in simulated time: two hand-offs of debounced publishes of one key to Block 13's path, seen as the `Action::SetDebounceTimer` each one issues, are never closer than the effective interval while the subscription stays `subscribed` (leaving `subscribed` closes the window, so the next publish leads again). The check is on hand-offs, not on frames: a trailing send can wait for room or a batch (D7, D8) and leave right after the next one. I5 counts debounce timers as subscription timers. I6 as in D6. Each new or amended invariant has a planted fault, as Block 16 requires, in the clock or the tap, never the client: a debounce timer the simulated clock fires before its delay (I12); a publish that waited in a window whose settle action is dropped before the checker (I6).
- **D17 Version, changelog and docs.** Additive, no version bump: new `Input` and `Action` variants on `#[non_exhaustive]` enums, a new code, a new behaviour triggered only by a field no OSS server sends (0.21.0's semver check passes; 46b's map items are `unstable`). Changelog `Unreleased`, "Added": "Publish debouncing as advised by the server (Centrifugo PRO): `Subscription::publish` and `publish_json` send the first value at once and the latest per interval, and each publish resolves with the result of the send that carried later data (Block 46). `codes::error::PUBLISH_DROPPED`; `machine::DebounceTimer`, `Input::DebounceTimerFired`, `Action::SetDebounceTimer` and `CancelDebounceTimer`, `Machine::with_publish_debounce`." 46b adds, prefixed "Unstable (`unstable` feature):", the map per-key debounce. 46c adds nothing. The README's "Calls" section gains a paragraph, marked Centrifugo PRO and untested against a real PRO server: what merges, what the futures report, that waiting data is dropped on leaving `subscribed` (D10), and, for data that must arrive, to use `Client::publish` (the documentation's own caveat).

Sources read (2026-11-09), with what each settles:

*centrifuge-js 63ed73e.* Its tests: `src/debounce.test.ts` (needs Centrifugo PRO; the latest value reaches the server), `src/debounce_publish_error.test.ts` (a failed trailing send raises no unhandled rejection), `src/debounce_reconnect.test.ts` ("pending debounced publish is cancelled on reconnect, not sent later").
- `src/subscription.ts:114-116`: `_debounceMs` and a `Map` of `{ data, dirty, timer }` per key.
- `:255-298` `_debouncedPublish`: with an entry for the key, the data is replaced, `dirty` set, the timer kept, and `{}` returned at once (`:256-262`). Without one, the data is sent at once and its real promise returned (`:293-297`), a timer of `_debounceMs` started (`:265`). When that timer fires with `dirty` set, the latest is sent, errors swallowed (`:275-278`), and a second timer started (`:280-290`); a second firing with `dirty` set calls `_debouncedPublish` again as a first publish. So one window per key at a time, a leading send and a trailing send, at most one send per interval; the timer is not reset by new publishes, which makes this a throttle with a leading and a trailing edge under the name "debounce".
- `:300-306` `_cancelDebounce`, `:308-313` `_cancelAllDebounce`, called when leaving `subscribed` (`:476` `_clearSubscribedState`, `:1097` `_setUnsubscribed`). Pending data is dropped; the promises it answered already resolved `{}`.
- `:573-575` (stream subscribe reply) and `:2626-2628` (map subscribe reply) set `_debounceMs` only when the field is truthy: an interval is never turned off by a later reply.
- `:2879-2883`: `Subscription.publish` debounces with key `''` after `await this._methodCall()`. `:2900-2902`: `MapSubscription.publish` debounces per key. `:2908-2910`: `MapSubscription.remove` cancels the key's pending publish, then sends the remove undebounced.
- `src/centrifuge.ts:566-567`, `:579-580`: `mapPublish` and `mapRemove` on the client are documented as not debounced ("prefer `sub.publish(key, data)` … it enforces the method-call guard and applies debounce configuration"). `Centrifuge.publish` is what the debounce calls, so it is undebounced too.

*`client.proto:629-631`:* "Interval in milliseconds. When > 0 the SDK should debounce client publications to this channel; the first one is not debounced."

*Centrifugo documentation* (read 2026-11-09): "the server returns the debounce interval in the subscribe result"; namespace option `client_publish_debounce_interval`, example `"50ms"`; "The debounce is applied when publishing via the subscription object"; "The first publish is never debounced"; "only the latest value is kept"; "For map subscriptions, debouncing is per key"; "For stream subscriptions, debouncing is per channel"; "On unsubscribe or disconnect, the SDK drops all pending publishes — nothing to clean up on the server"; "every `publish()` call resolves immediately"; "Do not use debouncing for data that must reliably reach the server"; only centrifuge-js supports it (SDK feature matrix). The page lists no server-side merging or enforcement. The Client SDK specification and the client protocol page do not mention debouncing (`client_api`, `client_protocol`).

*centrifuge library `7ac037196c95` (the version Centrifugo v6.10.1 pins):* `options.go:245-248`, `client.go:5101-5102` and `client_map.go:1062-1063` copy `ClientPublishDebounceInterval` into the subscribe reply as `publish_debounce`, in the stream reply and the map's live-phase reply. The library does nothing else with it: no enforcement on the publish path.

*centrifugal/centrifuge-rust 88d6edf, `docs/spec.md` and `docs/api.md` only (clean room):* debouncing is planned for phase 3 and undesigned (`docs/spec.md:86`, `:94`, `:1200`: "The core keeps `publish_debounce` from the subscribe reply (proto field 19), unused until then"; `docs/api.md:310`). No design to compare with.

*The feature therefore needs one server capability: the field.* Everything else is client-side; the interval is the only server input, and the server neither merges nor checks publishes.

Verified (Centrifugo v6.10.1 OSS, 2026-11-09, by the drafter and again by the reviewer; a raw websocket client against a container with `client.insecure` and a `cursors` namespace plus a `map` namespace, each with `client_publish_debounce_interval: "50ms"`):
- the server logs `unknown key in configuration file` for `channel.namespaces.[0].client_publish_debounce_interval`, and the same for `[1]`, and starts: the option is PRO only;
- a subscribe to `cursors:a` answers `{"id":2,"subscribe":{}}`, without `publish_debounce`; a map subscribe (`type` 1, `phase` 2, `limit` 2) on the empty channel answers `{"id":30,"subscribe":{"recoverable":true,"epoch":"…","type":1}}`, without it either;
- 5 publishes sent back to back to `cursors:a` get 5 replies and 5 publications, in order: nothing is merged or refused by the server.

`VERIFY:` nothing Centrifugo PRO does is observable here: the open-source server cannot send the field. As with channel compaction (Block 35), every scenario that needs a non-zero interval is @D or @E; the only @A scenario is the absence case. A PRO behaviour the documentation leaves open (whether PRO refuses or drops publishes that arrive inside the interval from a client that does not debounce) cannot be tested; Ferrifuge debounces as the proto says, so it never hands publishes over faster than the effective interval on a debounced path.

**Structural acceptance:**
- D2: unit tests on both codecs: `publish_debounce` decodes; absent and 0 mean none; a frame without it is unchanged byte for byte. Fuzz targets and seed corpus: `SubscribeResult` gains the field in the existing seeds.
- `start_call` is the only gate: a unit test that a `Client::publish` to the channel of a debounced subscription is sent at once, and a `CallRequest::Publish` through `add_subscription_call` with interval 0 is too.
- D5: `DebounceTimerFired` for an unknown `DebounceTimer` returns no action; every window opened is either cancelled or fired; `Action::SetDebounceTimer` count equals hand-offs (mutation: a window not cancelled on leaving `subscribed`). A machine without `with_publish_debounce` given an interval sends every publish and issues no debounce timer (mutation: the gate ignores the opt-in). `KeyedTimers::fired_all` on a paused tokio clock returns every timer due, and none not due; the driver feeds them before one flush.
- D10 and D12: mutations: a parked publish that survives a transition; a remove that does not close the window.
- D11: unit test for each clause.
- D13: `call_wait` is `Other` for a publish in a window and follows the trailing send's phase for its followers (mutation: a window reported as `Message`).
- D3: the trailing send does not meet the gate (mutation: a trailing send parked in its own window).
- D15: the Block 14 @P gates pass unchanged.
- Block 34's test passes with code 17's row; `Unreleased` entries present; `cargo semver-checks` passes on default features.
- `tests/support/fake_server.rs` gains a control to set `publish_debounce` on the next subscribe replies; the JSON and Protobuf replies carry it.

Value clause: As an app developer on Centrifugo PRO publishing fast-changing values over a subscription, I want the client to apply the server's debounce interval per channel or key, sending the first value at once and the latest per interval, with every publish reporting the server's answer for the value that replaced it, so that upstream traffic and server load fall without code of mine and without a publish claiming a success nobody gave.

**Exceptions introduced:**
- A later subscribe reply without an interval turns debouncing off (D2); centrifuge-js keeps the old one (`src/subscription.ts:573`, `:2626`). Block 0 precedence: `client.proto`, "When > 0".
- The interval is capped at `Config::timeout` (D2); `client.proto` and centrifuge-js set no cap. Block 13: a call never hangs.
- A publish that waits in a window resolves with the result of the send that replaced it, and fails with its error or as D10 says (D4, D10); centrifuge-js and the documentation resolve it at once with `{}`. The owner's decision ("Planned after Block 19", item 32).
- A publish whose future was dropped while later waiters depend on its value is still sent (D11), against Block 13's "never sent if it was queued": an earlier publish was replaced by that value.

## Block 47 — Shared poll subscriptions (unstable)

**Goal:** an application that shows live values for many items (prices, vote counts, statuses) tells the client which keys it follows; Centrifugo polls the application's backend once per key on behalf of every client and fans the changes out; the client tracks keys under signatures the backend issued, delivers each new version once with Block 15's guarantees, keeps its keys across reconnects without calling the backend for each device, and refreshes each signature as it expires; behind the non-default `unstable` feature. Source: parity item 30, design A ("Planned after Block 19": "Experimental APIs (items 29, 30, 33) are behind a non-default `unstable` feature, documented unstable and pinned to 63ed73e"; `ANALYSIS-PARITY.md`, branch `analysis/parity`, "30. Shared poll subscriptions": "Recommendation. A, its API documented as unstable"; reverses Block 0's exclusion, recorded in Block 0's "Reversed exclusions"); centrifuge-js 63ed73e `newSharedPollSubscription` (`src/centrifuge.ts:350`), `SharedPollSubscription` (`src/subscription.ts:2915-3084`), README.md:895-908 ("experimental and require Centrifugo >= v6.8.0"); Centrifugo v6.10.1 with centrifuge `7ac037196c95`, which it pins (`go.mod:18`).

The spec (`transports/client_api`, `transports/client_protocol`, read 2026-11-10) does not mention shared poll, `track` or `untrack`; the server documentation does (`docs/server/shared_poll`, read 2026-11-10: "the SDK resets all stored versions, triggering a one-time full resync" on a changed epoch). Its wire contract is `client.proto` (`SubscribeRequest.type` 4, `SubRefreshRequest.type` 1 and 2, `TrackBatch`, `KeyedItem`, `SubRefreshResult.items`, `Publication.key`, `removed`, `version`, lines 277-294, 557-564, 634-676); its behaviour is centrifuge-js 63ed73e, checked against the server.

**The feature is open source.** Centrifugo v6.10.1 OSS (`/api/info` reports "6.10.1 OSS") serves shared poll subscriptions completely; Verified below. What PRO adds is outside this client's contract (`docs/pro/shared_poll`, read 2026-11-10): `keep_latest_data`, a notification fast path, backpressure and a relay. Consequences: the items a track reply can carry need `keep_latest_data` (centrifuge `shared_poll.go:888-898`), so they run on @D only; every other path runs on a real server, delta compression included, since the refresh response's `prev_data` works on OSS (Verified).

**How @A tests it.** The config check requires a refresh endpoint on every shared poll namespace, and the only per-key write the server API offers is `shared_poll_publish` (versioned mode with `publish_enabled`). With the endpoint pointing at a port nothing listens on, the server tracks, reports refresh errors in its log and delivers what `shared_poll_publish` sends (Verified). So @A covers subscribing, tracking, versions, untracking, reconnects, limits and refused signatures; @B, with the test backend answering refreshes (`ProxyBackend` gains `/shared_poll_refresh`), covers the versionless default mode, backend removals, the epoch flip and `prev_data` deltas; @D covers what a server cannot be made to produce.

**Dependencies:** Blocks 0 (references, precedence, Components rule, test layers), 2 (backoff formula), 3 (1009 ends the client), 7 (Protobuf, protocol faults), 8 (transports, emulation), 9 (subscription lifecycle, registry, unsubscribe while in flight), 10 (tokens, `sub_refresh`, unsubscribe codes, resubscribe backoff), 11 (2502, 3014), 13 (write queue, reply deadlines), 14 (marginal cost of a subscription), 15 (delivered means taken, in-order handling, read-ahead, withdrawal, errors past 256), 18 (the frame limits of the server), 19 (fossil delta, the inbound limit, failure outcomes), 20 (semver check, docs.rs, changelog), 21 (logging, redacting `Debug`), 26 (the emulation envelope), 29 (message size), 30 (`ready()`), 31 (statistics, delta statistics), 32 (`set_data`), 33 (`close()`), 34 (codes table), 36 (optimistic subscriptions, automatic batching), 37 (test constructors), 38 (JSON helpers), 39 (one active stream), 41 (handlers, delivery modes, deadlock detection), 44 (browser target, `MaybeSend`), 45 (the `unstable` feature, one registry, `MaybeSend` handles), 46 (opaque timers on the core), 49 (I13, I14, D10).

**Out of scope:**
- a client publishing to a shared poll channel: `publish` on such a channel gets 103 (Verified), and centrifuge-js's `SharedPollSubscription` has no publish (`src/centrifuge.ts:56-62`);
- `get_state`, `get_data`, `since`, `positioned`, `recoverable`, `join_leave`, tag filters and channel compaction on shared poll subscriptions: centrifuge-js's `SharedPollSubscriptionOptions` has none of them (`src/types.ts:791-816`), and its subscribe command returns before setting any of them (`src/subscription.ts:968-972`). `data` and `set_data` stay;
- `history()`: not on the type in centrifuge-js (`src/centrifuge.ts:39-44`, `:56-62`), and the server answers 108 (Verified);
- server-side shared poll subscriptions: centrifuge reaches the shared poll flow only from a client's subscribe command with `type` 4 (`client_shared_poll.go:12`); a `ConnectResult.subs` entry or `Subscribe` push is handled as today;
- a client-side mirror of the values (an `items()` accessor): the application keeps its own, as with centrifuge-js;
- the server API's `shared_poll_publish` other than in tests (a backend's concern; `ServerApi` gains it);
- the in-memory server double (Block 37), the chaos runners (Block 16), the trace replay (Block 42) and the real-server chaos and soak runs (Blocks 51, 52): none models shared poll subscriptions while they are unstable, which the double's rustdoc says (D19);
- computing a signature: the backend does, the client only carries it (`ANALYSIS-PARITY.md`, "the client checks no signature ... so no cryptography is involved").

This block reverses Block 0's exclusion of shared poll subscriptions and the exclusions of Blocks 9, 11 and 19 that name it (owner decision, 2026-11-06, late, item 30); Block 0's "Reversed exclusions" gains its row. It amends Block 15's "Withdrawal" (D9), Block 34 D1 and adds rows to Block 34's tables (D14), and Block 31's `publications_delivered` (D13), as listed after this block.

| 47e | As an app developer using handlers, typed JSON, test constructors or the browser target, I want shared poll subscriptions there too, so that they fit the rest of my code | "A shared poll subscription handler receives the events in order", "A test builds shared poll events without a server", "A browser client tracks a key and receives its updates" |

**Decisions** (reviewer, 2026-11-10, delegated by the owner, after a three-amigos round table on the draft):

- **D1 Design A, behind `unstable`.** A handle type of its own, as the analysis recommends and as Block 45 D1 decided for map subscriptions: centrifuge-js 63ed73e has its own class and registry accessors (`SharedPollSubscription`, `src/subscription.ts:2915`; `getSharedPollSubscription`, `removeSharedPollSubscription`, `sharedPollSubscriptions`, `src/centrifuge.ts:380`, `:410`, `:429`); `SubscriptionEvent` matches do not grow variants a stream subscription never emits; `track` exists only where a key means something. centrifugal/centrifuge-rust `docs/spec.md` (88d6edf, §9.11, as quoted in Block 45 D1) plans the same split. Everything public this block adds is `#[cfg(feature = "unstable")]` with `#[cfg_attr(docsrs, doc(cfg(feature = "unstable")))]`, except the code constants of D14, and its rustdoc opens with: "Unstable: requires the `unstable` feature, follows centrifuge-js 63ed73e and Centrifugo's experimental shared poll subscriptions (v6.8.0 and later), and may change in any minor release."

- **D2 Public API** (adapter, both targets):
  - `Client::shared_poll_subscription_builder(&self, channel: impl Into<String>) -> SharedPollSubscriptionBuilder`, `Client::new_shared_poll_subscription(&self, channel) -> Result<SharedPollSubscription, SubscriptionError>`; `get_shared_poll_subscription(&self, &str) -> Option<SharedPollSubscription>`, `shared_poll_subscriptions(&self) -> Vec<SharedPollSubscription>`, `remove_shared_poll_subscription(&self, &SharedPollSubscription)` (unsubscribes first, as Block 9's removal).
  - One registry for all kinds (Block 45 D2, centrifuge-js `_subs`, `src/centrifuge.ts:353`): creating any subscription on a channel already taken by any kind fails with `SubscriptionError::AlreadyExists`; `get_subscription` and `subscriptions()` list stream subscriptions only, `get_map_subscription` and `map_subscriptions()` map subscriptions only, these only shared poll subscriptions.
  - `SharedPollSubscriptionBuilder`: `token`, `get_token` (Block 10), `data` (Block 9), `min_resubscribe_delay`, `max_resubscribe_delay` (Block 10 defaults), `get_signature` (D6), `delta(DeltaFormat)` (D10), `max_delta_bases_bytes(NonZeroUsize)` (D11), `max_track_frame_bytes(NonZeroUsize)` (D7), `handler` (D15), `build() -> Result<SharedPollSubscription, SubscriptionError>`.
  - `SharedPollSubscription` (`Clone`, `Debug`, `PartialEq`, `Eq` as `Subscription`): `channel()`, `state() -> SubscriptionState`, `events() -> impl Stream<Item = SharedPollSubscriptionEvent> + MaybeSend + Unpin + use<>` (one active stream, Block 15), `set_handler`, `held_events()`, `subscribe()`, `unsubscribe()`, `ready()` (Block 30), `track(keys: impl IntoIterator<Item = impl Into<String>>)`, `track_with_signature(items: impl IntoIterator<Item = SharedPollTrackItem>, signature: impl Into<String>)`, `untrack(keys: impl IntoIterator<Item = impl Into<String>>)`, `tracked_keys() -> Vec<String>`, `presence()`, `presence_stats()` (centrifuge-js `CommonSurface`, `src/centrifuge.ts:39-44`), `set_data` (Block 32), `delta_statistics()` (D13).
  - `track`, `track_with_signature`, `untrack` are synchronous and return nothing: fire-and-forget, as centrifuge-js ("Fire-and-forget ... returns void and never throws", `src/subscription.ts:2914-2933`, `:3055-3057`); failures come as `Error` events and synthetic removals (D7). Being synchronous they cannot deadlock from a handler and need no `WouldDeadlock` path (Block 41 D6).
  - `pub struct SharedPollTrackItem { pub key: String, pub version: u64 }` (`#[non_exhaustive]`, `new(key, version)`), and `pub struct SharedPollSignature { pub keys: Vec<String>, pub signature: String }` (`#[non_exhaustive]`, `new`), its `Debug` redacting the signature (D16).
  - `pub enum SharedPollSubscriptionEvent`, `#[non_exhaustive]`: `Subscribing { code, reason }`, `Subscribed(Subscribed)`, `Unsubscribed { code, reason }`, `Update(SharedPollUpdate)`, `Error(ClientError)`, with `name()` as `SubscriptionEvent::name` ("update"). `Subscribed` is Block 11's struct, with no stream position (a shared poll subscription has none).
  - `pub struct SharedPollUpdate { pub key: String, pub data: Vec<u8>, pub removed: bool, pub version: Option<u64> }`, `#[non_exhaustive]`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`, with Block 21's redacting `Debug` (data as its length; the key shown, as `MapEntry`). centrifuge-js `SharedPollUpdateContext` (`src/types.ts:749-760`). A removal's `data` is empty and its `version` `None` (`src/subscription.ts:2864-2869`; Verified: the server's removal push has neither). `version` is `None` for an absent or zero `version` (`client.proto`, `KeyedItem.version`: 0 means no version is known).
  - `ErrorKind` (non-exhaustive) gains `Track`, `Untrack` and `SignatureRefresh`, carrying centrifuge-js's error context `type` (`src/subscription.ts:1905`, `:1951`, `:2083`).
  - Not adopted: centrifuge-js's `publication` event alongside each `update` (`src/subscription.ts:1167-1173`), as Block 45 D2 decided for maps (Exceptions).

- **D3 Core.** One registry (`SubscriptionId` shared): a subscription has a kind, stream, map or shared poll; a shared poll subscription has `SharedPollSubscriptionOptions` (new, `#[non_exhaustive]`, unstable) and its state of D5, both boxed beside `map` under `unstable` (`Option<Box<...>>`, as Block 45's `MapFlow`), so a stream subscription pays a pointer (Block 14, "Marginal cost of a subscription"). `Machine::add_shared_poll_subscription(channel, SharedPollSubscriptionOptions) -> Result<SubscriptionId, SubscriptionError>`; the existing inputs (`Subscribe`, `Unsubscribe`, `EventTaken`, token and data answers) serve it, and its subscribe uses `SubscriptionTimer::Resubscribe` and `SubscribeReply` as any kind does. New, unstable: `Input::TrackKeys`, `Input::TrackKeysWithSignature`, `Input::UntrackKeys`, `Input::SignatureFetched { subscription, request, result }`, `Input::SharedPollTimerFired(SharedPollTimer)`, `Input::SharedPollRefreshFired(SubscriptionId)`; `Action::EmitSharedPollSubscription(EventId, SubscriptionId, SharedPollSubscriptionEvent)`, `Action::FetchSignature { subscription, request, keys }`, `Action::SetSharedPollTimer(SharedPollTimer, Duration)`, `Action::CancelSharedPollTimer(SharedPollTimer)`, `Action::SetSharedPollRefresh(SubscriptionId, Duration)` and `Action::CancelSharedPollRefresh(SubscriptionId)`, the owner holding one signature refresh timer per subscription that only moves earlier, so the refresh runs at the earliest deadline (D7) without a clock in the core. Every enum gaining a variant is `#[non_exhaustive]` (Block 45 D3, `src/machine.rs:502`, `:746`). `SharedPollTimer` is an opaque `Copy` number never reused by a machine, the driver holding them in `KeyedTimers<SharedPollTimer>`, as `DebounceTimer` (Block 46 D5): track and untrack reply deadlines and the retries, per request or per retry kind, none of which fits the exhaustive `Timer` and `SubscriptionTimer` (`src/machine.rs:421`, `:453`), which stay unchanged. A machine without shared poll subscriptions sets no such timer, so no `with_...` switch is needed (Block 46 D5's reason does not apply: an owner adds these subscriptions only through the unstable call).
  - The wire model (`src/wire.rs`, `src/json.rs`, `src/protobuf.rs`) gains `Publication.version` (16), `SubRefreshRequest.type` (3), `track` (4), `untrack` (5), `KeyedItem` (`key`, `version`), `TrackBatch` (`signature`, `items`), and `SubRefreshResult.items` (3); `SubscribeRequest.type` and `SubscribeResult.type` exist since Block 45. Zero and empty values are not encoded (a key at version 0 goes as `{"key":"k"}`, `src/subscription.ts:1691`, Verified), so existing commands are unchanged byte for byte (unit tests on both codecs).

- **D4 The subscribe flow.** `subscribe { channel, type: 4, token, data, delta }` (`src/subscription.ts:968-972`), in the connect frame when it fits (Block 36, as any subscribe). No recovery fields ever. The reply is a `SubscribeResult` with `type` 4, an optional `epoch`, optional `expires` and `ttl`, optional `delta` (centrifuge `client_shared_poll.go:87-139`; Verified). On it the subscription becomes `subscribed`, emits `Subscribed`, and sends the replay of D8.
  - A reply whose `type` is not 4 ends the subscription: the client sends an unsubscribe command and emits `Unsubscribed` with code 8 "shared poll subscriptions not supported", without subscribing again by itself. Block 45 D15's reason holds (a server before v6.8.0 ignores `type` and grants a stream subscription); centrifuge-js does not check it (Exceptions).
  - Subscribe errors follow Block 9 and Block 10 unchanged: 109 drops the token and resubscribes; temporary or below 100 emits an `Error` and resubscribes after the backoff; any other unsubscribes with its code (a namespace of another type answers 108, a stream subscribe to a shared poll namespace 107, a missing token 103, Verified). `105` "already subscribed" is a plain permanent error.

- **D5 State per subscription** (centrifuge-js `src/subscription.ts:119-153`), in the core:
  - **`tracked`**: key to version (0 when none is known), in insertion order.
  - **`signatures`**: the library of `(keys, signature)` the client holds, each entry the exact key list its signature covers.
  - **`epoch`**: `None` until the first subscribe reply after `set_unsubscribed` (a subscription starts cold), then the last reply's epoch, an absent one as `""` (D8).
  - **`untrack_pending`**: per key, the untrack requests not yet answered, and the inline untracks (D7) of the key since its frame until a later track request carrying the key is accepted, or, once no frame carrying it inline awaits its reply and no held signature covers the key, until an untrack request of the key sent then is answered (D10; centrifuge `handleUntrack` answers after the channel's track requests in progress, waiting up to 5 s); empty when not `subscribed`.
  - **`tracked` and `signatures` persist** when the subscription leaves `subscribed` for `subscribing` (transport lost, server unsubscribe from 2500, delta failure, resubscribe backoff), as the JS comment says, "avoids hitting getSignature for every client during mass reconnect storms" (`src/subscription.ts:486-491`). They are cleared, with `epoch`, in `set_unsubscribed` (`:1088-1093`), so `unsubscribe()` and a removal start cold.
  - **Version moves when taken** (Block 15): a key's version moves to a publication's `version` when its `Update` is taken, and a track or replay built while such an event is in flight uses the version it would set (Block 41 D3); a panic in its handler voids that move as it voids a stream position (Block 41 D3, D4): the version goes back unless another step changed it since, so the next replay asks for the value again. Epoch resets (D8) apply to the versions held. A removal ends its key when it is handled, not when it is taken (D9).

- **D6 Signatures** (`src/types.ts:777-789`, `:800-808`; `src/subscription.ts:2934-3047`):
  - `get_signature`, on the builder, is an async callback built like `get_token` (Block 10): `Fn(Vec<String>) -> impl Future<Output = Result<SharedPollSignature, TokenError>>`, `MaybeSend` on both targets, polled beside the core, so a slow backend blocks no ping or call (Blocks 1, 10; Block 49 row S6 stands). `TokenError::Unauthorized` is the "user may no longer use the subscription" case (`src/types.ts:805-807`).
  - **`track(keys)`** stores each key at `max(existing, 0)`; empty sets are no-ops (`:2935`). Subscribed, it requests a signature for those keys; not subscribed, it only stores them (the replay asks for what lacks one, `:2988-2993`). Each `Action::FetchSignature` carries a request number; an answer to an abandoned request (the subscription left `subscribed` meanwhile) changes nothing (I13's rule; `:2995-2997`).
  - **`track_with_signature(items, signature)`** stores each key at the higher of its version and the one held (`:2953-2960`), adds `(keys, signature)` to the library (dropping entries it fully covers, `_addSharedPollSignature`, `:1896-1900`), and when subscribed sends the batch as given; not subscribed, the replay sends it.
  - **`untrack(keys)`** removes the keys from `tracked` at once, drops library entries whose every key is untracked (`:3063-3065`), and sends an untrack command if subscribed. An empty key set sends nothing (Verified the server answers 107 to one; centrifuge-js would send it).
  - **What the callback returns** may be a subset: keys in the request and not in the result are revoked, each giving a synthetic removal `Update` and an untrack command (`:3001-3026`); the result's keys are then tracked as a batch whose items include any key since untracked, sent in that request's `untrack` field too, since the signature covers the exact list (`_signedBatch`, `:1639-1652`; server: the signature is over the keys in order, `client_keyed.go:72`, `internal/client/track_signature.go`, Verified "key order swapped" is refused). A result with no key still tracked sends nothing. A result whose batch is over the budget by D7's worst-case cost (more keys than asked for) is refused before the library and the wire with an `Error` of code 12, of the kind a failed fetch on that path reports, its keys staying tracked, and retried as a failed fetch.
  - **An explicit batch over the budget.** `track_with_signature` sends its batch as given when it fits. One over `max_track_frame_bytes` by D7's worst-case cost is refused before it enters the library or the wire: an `Error` of kind `Track`, code 12 "track batch over max_track_frame_bytes", and its keys untracked with synthetic removal `Update`s (D7, D9), since a single batch cannot be split and sending it would end the client.
  - **Refreshing without a callback.** With `track_with_signature` only, refreshing an expiring signature is the application's job: it calls `track_with_signature` again before `exp`. Otherwise the server drops the keys silently after `exp` plus `track_expired_extra_delay` (no removal is pushed, Verified) and `tracked_keys` still lists them; the rustdoc and the README say so.
  - **A key set with no callback:** `track(keys)` without `get_signature` emits an `Error` of kind `Track`, code 14, "get_signature callback required for track(keys)" (`:2978-2984`), and the keys stay tracked (the next replay reports it again, `:2196-2201`).
  - **Callback failure:** `Unauthorized` unsubscribes with code 1 "unauthorized" (`:3036-3039`); any other error emits an `Error` of kind `Track` (track path) or `SignatureRefresh` (refresh and replay paths), code 14 (`:3041-3046`, `:2085-2089`), and retries after 5 s to 30 s (D7): on the track and replay paths, a fetch for the tracked keys that no held signature or fetch in flight covers (D8 phase 2), held signatures not resent; a refresh retries the refresh.
  - **Chunks (divergence).** A key set whose single batch would exceed `max_track_frame_bytes` by D7's worst-case cost is asked for in chunks, each a separate `Action::FetchSignature`, one at a time in key order, each chunk sized by D7's worst-case cost (the signature's length counted as 128 until known) so that its batch can be replayed alone whatever versions it later holds. The chunks of one request are collected and handled as one result (revocations, tracking, and for a refresh the library swap of D7). A chunk whose fetch fails fails the whole request as above; what the other chunks returned is dropped. Reason: a single batch cannot be split (the signature covers its exact list), and a frame over the server's `websocket.message_size_limit` (65 536 by default, Block 18 D5) closes the connection with 1009, which Block 3 turns into `disconnected` code 3 for the whole client (Verified with 1800 keys of 44 bytes, about 99 KB). Nothing in centrifuge-js avoids it: a refresh of a large key set kills the client hours after start, the moment the first expiry fires.

- **D7 Track requests, replies and errors** (`_sendTrackRequest`, `_handleTrackResponse`, `_handleTrackError`, `src/subscription.ts:1655-1735`, `:1789-1836`, `:1902-1937`):
  - A track request is one `sub_refresh { channel, type: 1, track: [{ signature, items: [{ key, version }] }], untrack }`. Frames: a request's batches are split so that no frame exceeds `max_track_frame_bytes` (default 60 000, centrifuge-js's `maxBytes`, `:1663`; below `websocket.message_size_limit` and emulation's `max_request_body_size`, 65 536 each, Block 18 D5; rustdoc and README say an operator who lowers either lowers this). The cost of a frame is computed for the worst encoding, not by centrifuge-js's estimate (`:1666-1676`, 16 bytes per item, unsafe once versions are carried): JSON inside the JSON string of an emulation request (Block 26), each version at `u64::MAX`; per item the key's doubly JSON-escaped length and 48; per batch 40 and the signature's length; per frame 256 and the channel's doubly escaped length; per inline untrack key its doubly escaped length and 6. Protobuf is never larger. Verified: 2491 keys of 8 bytes at version 1 000 000, within centrifuge-js's estimate, are 92 KB and close the websocket with 1009, and a track of 62 882 bytes over emulation gets HTTP 413; two frames of 900 keys each are accepted. A key of the request's `untrack` goes only in the `untrack` field of the frame carrying its batch: the server ignores an inline untrack of a key it does not track yet, and a later frame would track it again. Frames fill in order: a batch joins the current frame when it and its untracks fit by the costs above; otherwise it starts the next frame, taking as many of its untracks as fit. The untracks that do not fit are untracked by the `stale` rule below once that frame's reply is read, in requests split as below, sent before the request's next frame (Exceptions). Frames go one after the other, and a failing frame stops the rest (`:1721`, "Sequential dispatch"), a permanent error untracking the keys of every frame not accepted (`:1686`).
  - An untrack request is `sub_refresh { channel, type: 2, untrack: [keys] }`. On every path that sends one (`untrack()`, a revoked key, a stale key of a track reply, a permanent error, a batch refused for its size (D6), an inline untrack of a key no held signature covers (D5)), its keys are split over as many requests as the budget needs, each within `max_track_frame_bytes` by the costs above (per key its doubly escaped length and 6, per frame 256 and the channel's doubly escaped length), since a single oversized command is sent alone (Block 18 D5) and would end the client with 1009. A key's `untrack_pending` (D5, D10) counts the request it went in, and a request that fails reports its own `Error` of kind `Untrack`.
  - A single batch over `max_track_frame_bytes` never reaches the wire (D6).
  - Both are the client's own commands: they bypass the write queue's admission as subscribe and unsubscribe do (Block 13), are bounded by `Config::timeout` each (Block 15's rule pauses the deadline while a reply waits to be handled), and join automatic batching (Block 36) like any command.
  - **Replies are handled in order** (Block 15): a track reply can carry `items` and its pushes follow it on the connection (centrifuge `client_keyed.go:435-440`). `items` are handled as publications (D9). Keys of the request no longer tracked (`stale`) get an untrack command (`:1815-1821`). `expires` schedules the refresh (below). A track reply of an earlier subscription is dropped (`:1791-1793`; I13).
  - **Errors** (`:1902-1937`), each emitting an `Error` of kind `Track` first:
    - **109:** a consolidated refresh of the signatures (below) (`:1920-1923`); without a callback nothing more happens (the `Error` was reported). A 109 answering the track request of a refresh is a failure of that refresh and retries after 5 s to 30 s, so a backend signing expired signatures, or a clock behind the server's by more than the grace, cannot make a device loop on it; centrifuge-js refreshes again at once (Exceptions).
    - **Temporary, below 100, or a reply deadline on websocket:** after a backoff of 1 s to 15 s, the replay of D8 runs (`:1926-1929`).
    - **Any other:** the keys of the request are untracked, locally and by an untrack command, and each still-tracked key gives a synthetic removal `Update` (`:1940-1966`). 103 (invalid signature) and 106 (limit, Verified) land here.
    - An untrack error emits an `Error` of kind `Untrack` only (`:3072-3075`).
  - **Signature refresh** (`_sharedPollRefreshSignature`, `:1973-2100`): a reply with `expires` makes the refresh run at the earliest deadline it has seen, one timer per subscription (`now + ttl`, or `now + 1 s` when `ttl` is 0 or absent: a signature accepted within the server's 5 s grace, Verified; `:1830-1835`; the n-th such reply in a row (n ≥ 2) backs off by Block 2's formula at attempt n − 1, bounds 1 s and 15 s, the attempt count reset by a reply with a positive `ttl`, so a backend that keeps issuing expired signatures is not polled every second, Exceptions). When it fires, with a callback and at least one key tracked: a fetch for every tracked key (chunked, D6); one at a time, and a tracked key not covered by the fetch in flight runs another once it ends (`:1978-1985`, `:2008-2011`). The result revokes as in D6, replaces the library with the new entries plus any entry still needed for keys outside it (`:2034-2046`), and is tracked. A failure retries after 5 s to 30 s (`:2091`). The refresh guard and target reset when the subscription leaves `subscribed` (`:477-485`).
  - Backoff uses Block 2's formula with those bounds (`src/utils.ts:30-36`); each retry timer has its own attempt counter, reset on success and on leaving `subscribed` (`:128-134`, `:477-479`).
  - Server: a key whose signature expired is dropped silently after `exp` plus `track_expired_extra_delay` (25 s by default: centrifuge `client.go:1467-1471`, `config.go:358`, the check `client_keyed.go:724`; centrifugo docs; Verified, no removal pushed), so refreshing at the expiry, within the grace period, loses no key, and the client never sees a removal for it.

- **D8 Replay after subscribe** (`_sharedPollReplayTrack`, `:2117-2230`). On every `subscribed` (first subscribe and each resubscribe), in the step that makes it so:
  - If `epoch` is `Some` and differs from the reply's, an absent reply `epoch` being `""`, every held version is set to 0 before anything is sent; `epoch` then takes the reply's value. Versions given before the first subscribe of a subscription are kept, whatever its epoch: `epoch` is `None` then. Reason (Verified): the server's versions restart lower after the channel's state is recreated or the backend's epoch changes (2500, D13), so a version held from before suppresses every value until a higher one comes, and a version sent as 0 gets the current value. centrifuge-js's rule resets only when its kept epoch is non-empty (`:579-587`), which leaves the first epoch a backend reports suppressed: Verified, a kept empty epoch with held version 3 gets nothing after the flip to version 1; the server's comment and its documentation ask for version 0 (centrifuge `shared_poll.go:944-946`) (Exceptions).
  - Phase 1: every library entry is sent as a batch of one track request with its original key list and the current versions (0 for a key since untracked), with those untracked keys placed as D7 says (Verified inline untrack frees slots). A key left out for the budget is tracked on the server from its frame until its untrack: the server counts it against `max_keys_per_connection` and may send its value, which D9 drops. All-or-nothing on the server (`Handler.OnTrack`, one bad batch refuses the whole request, Verified).
  - Phase 2: tracked keys with no library entry go to one fetch (chunked, D6); no callback emits the error 14 of D6. A failure retries after 5 s to 30 s (`:2240-2245`).
  - No `get_signature` runs for keys already in the library, so a mass reconnect does not touch the backend while its signatures stay valid.

- **D9 Publications** (`_handlePublication`, `:1109-1200`), for a push or a track reply item, in this order:
  - **Not tracked:** a key not in `tracked` is dropped silently, as centrifuge-js does for the race its comment describes (a replay carries untracked keys until the inline untrack is applied, `:1143-1153`), but before decoding, so an untracked key creates no delta base (Exceptions: centrifuge-js decodes first, `:1122-1138`).
  - **Duplicate:** a publication with a `version`, not `removed`, not newer than the version held (when that is above 0) is dropped (`:1110-1118`; Verified the server repeats the same version after a re-track from 0). With delta on it is decoded first, whole or delta, and becomes its key's base, replacing any: the server's next delta applies to the last value it sent (centrifuge `keyedWritePublication`), which after a re-track can be an older value sent late.
  - **Decoding:** delta (D10).
  - **Delivery:** one `Update { key, data, removed, version }`, in order (Block 15). Within one message (the items of one track reply) the version check compares against what the earlier items would set.
  - **Removals.** A `removed` publication ends the key when it is handled: the key leaves `tracked`, its delta base goes (D10), and the `Update { removed: true }` is queued; a synthetic removal does the same (D6, D7). A removal `Update` is never withdrawn (amends Block 15, "Withdrawal"), as no later step would bring it back, and tracking the key again later is unaffected; centrifuge-js ends it when it is delivered (`:1194-1196`), which on a client-side reason would lose it here. A removal of a key no longer tracked is dropped by the first rule, and a publication with no key is the empty key, dropped by it too.
  - **Delivered means taken:** an `Update` of a value not taken when the subscription leaves `subscribed` for a client-side reason is withdrawn (Block 15), and the key's version did not move, so the replay asks from the old version and the server sends it again (Verified: a held version equal to the latest gets no redelivery, version 0 does). A connection closed by the server holds its pending events as Block 15 says.

- **D10 Delta compression** (Block 19, per key):
  - `delta(DeltaFormat::Fossil)` sends `delta: "fossil"` on the subscribe; the reply's `delta` says whether it is on (Verified on an `allowed_delta_types: ["fossil"]` namespace; absent otherwise).
  - With delta on, every publication's data is a JSON string on the JSON protocol (Verified: the first, whole, and later ones) unwrapped per Block 19 D7. Bases are per key: the data of the last publication handled for that key, deleted when the key stops being tracked (an untrack, a removal, a permanent error). On a new subscribe every base is dropped, so Block 19 D5's "cleared at each subscribe" holds, unlike map subscriptions (Block 45 D9): each track resets the server's per-key `deltaReady`, so the first publication after a track, a replay or a signature refresh is whole (`client_keyed.go:37-41`, `:319-324`, Verified). centrifuge-js keeps the map across a resubscribe, where it is simply overwritten by the whole first publication (`:1122-1138`), and after an untrack (`:3058-3066`); Ferrifuge frees it.
  - **A delta for a key with no base while `untrack_pending` names that key** is dropped: neither delivered nor a failure. On one connection the server answers commands and pushes in order, so a delta it sent before handling the untrack can reach a client that has already tracked the key again and dropped its base; the track reply and the whole first publication follow it (D7). Any other delta with no base is Block 19's failure.
  - Failures: Block 19 D3 and D8 unchanged (`Error` of kind `Delta`, code 15, then `Subscribing` code 2, an unsubscribe command and a resubscribe after the backoff); the resubscribe replays and each key comes back whole. On OSS a delta exists only when the backend's refresh returns `prev_data` (Verified); the rustdoc says so.

- **D11 Memory bound** (what a server can grow):
  - **Events and messages.** Block 15's read-ahead and Block 29's per-message limit bound what is read; track replies are ordinary messages. Block 15's "Errors past 256" bounds the retry `Error` events a stuck backend can add.
  - **Delta bases.** A base exists only for a tracked key (D9, D10) and each within Block 19 D6's limit, so the server can grow only values, not keys. `max_delta_bases_bytes`, default 64 MiB (Block 19 D6's inbound limit), bounds their total; a key whose base would pass it ends the subscription: the client sends an unsubscribe command and emits `Unsubscribed` with code 7 "shared poll delta bases too large", and does not subscribe again by itself, since every resubscribe would end the same way (as `unsubscribed` 5, Block 45 D5); the publication that passes the bound is not delivered. centrifuge-js has no bound (Exceptions).
  - **Tracked keys and the signature library** grow only by the application's calls and its backend's answers, not by the server: a publication of an unknown key is dropped (D9). Entries with no tracked key are dropped (D6, D7). They are not bounded (as Block 15's "Events caused by application calls"), and the rustdoc says so, with the server's `max_keys_per_connection` (5000 by default) as the usual limit. Tracked keys cost memory per key, not per subscription; `perf_footprint` reports it (Structural acceptance), and Block 14's 2 KiB per subscription holds for a subscription tracking no key.

- **D12 Emulated transports** (`_sharedPollSerial`, `_sharedPollRequestFailed`, `src/subscription.ts:1741-1763`). Over `http_stream` and `sse` each request is a separate HTTP request the server may handle in any order, so a subscription's track and untrack requests go one at a time, in the order made, each waiting for its reply; a request of an earlier subscription is dropped when its turn comes. The next subscribe of the subscription waits for the queue to drain (`:640-642`). A track or untrack reply deadline passing over emulation makes the client reconnect with `connecting` code 3 "shared poll request timeout", since whether the keys are tracked is unknown (`:1758-1763`). Verified: `sub_refresh` track over `http_stream` and over `sse` with the emulation endpoint delivers the same reply and pushes as websocket. It lands in 47a, whose scenarios run over `http_stream` and `sse`.

- **D13 Tokens, data, statistics** (Blocks 10, 31, 32): the subscription token goes on the subscribe; an expiring subscription (`expires`, `ttl` in the reply) is refreshed with `sub_refresh` type 0 as Block 10 (Verified), its timers kept apart from the signature refresh's. `data` and `set_data` go on the subscribe. 2502 drops the token unconditionally and 3014 only where a token callback exists (Block 11), and both drop every delta base; `tracked`, `signatures` and versions stay, and the next reply's `epoch` decides (`_invalidateState`, `:514-530`, with no position to reset, so Block 11's sentinel epoch does not apply). `Statistics::subscriptions` counts shared poll subscriptions (one registry), and `publications_delivered` counts each `Update` of a publication taken; a synthetic removal counts as none. `delta_statistics()` counts whole and delta publications (Block 19, `:1128-1136`).

- **D14 Codes** (Block 34): `codes::error::SHARED_POLL_GET_SIGNATURE` = 14 "get_signature callback required ..." or the callback's error text (centrifuge-js's value, `src/codes.ts:15`); `codes::unsubscribed::SHARED_POLL_DELTA_BASES_TOO_LARGE` = 7 "shared poll delta bases too large" (D11) and `SHARED_POLL_NOT_SUPPORTED` = 8 "shared poll subscriptions not supported" (D4). Not behind `unstable`, for Block 45 D12's reason (`cargo doc` with default features resolves every constant); their documentation says only shared poll subscriptions (`unstable`) use them. Code 12 (`BAD_CONFIGURATION`) also reports a batch refused for its size (D6): its row's Cause gains it. Block 34's tables gain them, and the "Server codes" table and D1 change as listed after this block.

Block 39: no `updates()` view. Block 38: `SharedPollUpdate::json<T>()`, an empty removal yielding an error as `Publication::json` does. Block 37: under `test-util` and `unstable`, `SharedPollUpdate::new(key, data)`, `SharedPollUpdate::removal(key)` and setters.

A unit test (structural acceptance) covers it, since the runners do not model shared poll (D19; Block 49 row C2's class).

One @W scenario, on the browser harness's server with the @A namespace of D18 (the dead proxy endpoint and `shared_poll_publish`), so the harness needs no refresh backend; the relay gains two control requests, one signing a key and one calling `shared_poll_publish`, which a page cannot call (no CORS, and the API key stays out of the page).
